Evidence discipline

Methodology

A broad, source-linked sweep of disclosed 2027 binaries, with uncertainty shown rather than buried and known timing gaps kept visible.

HARDExact date from FDA or an event organizer.
GUIDANCECompany-guided window such as Q1 or H2.
INFERREDDerived from registry or submission timelines; highest slip risk.

Universe

The v4.0 dataset contains 1,128 source-linked records across 300 tickers with qualifying clinical or regulatory events. Conference rows are excluded from the ticker-with-events count.

Evidence order

SEC filings → FDA and regulatory records → ClinicalTrials.gov and History of Changes → conference programs → company PRs and decks → genuine wires and verbatim-source fallbacks.

PDUFAs: an event is labeled a PDUFA only when the FDA has accepted the application for review. Filings still awaiting acceptance are not shown as PDUFAs.

What counts

Every clinical data readout regardless of stage; IND, NDA, and BLA filings and acceptances; PDUFAs; posted AdComs; other binary regulatory decisions; and major conferences with stock-relevant data. No date is invented: unguided timelines receive no entry.

Dataset shape

v4.0 contains 1,128 records: 208 Phase 3, 333 Phase 2, 218 Phase 1, 9 preclinical, and 360 regulatory-or-conference records without a clinical phase. Event types include 728 readouts, 43 PDUFAs, 28 NDA filings, 25 BLA filings, 15 INDs, 48 other regulatory events, 2 CHMP opinions, 2 MAA filings, 1 device regulatory decision, 27 HTA decisions, 5 M&A closes, 2 pricing decisions, 1 litigation milestone, 2 key patent expiries, 1 milestone payment, 1 biosimilar launch, 1 biosimilar decision, and 196 conferences.

Date quality is 253 hard, 403 guidance, and 472 inferred. Every row carries a last-checked date.

Impact ratings

Every event carries an impact rating — high, medium, or low — answering one question: how significant could this event be for the company involved? It is an estimate of an event’s binary significance from a published, mechanical formula. It is not a prediction of how the stock will move. A “high” rating does not mean the stock will rise or fall; it means the outcome matters a lot to the company’s value, so the price reaction could be large either way. A “low” rating means the event is unlikely to change the investment picture much, even if the outcome surprises.

The rating starts from the kind of event — approval decisions, Phase 3 readouts, EU opinions, device decisions, and mergers start high; filings, Phase 2 readouts, label expansions, and pricing decisions start medium; early-stage clearances, Phase 1 readouts, and conferences start low — then adjusts for company size. Large companies step down a notch, since one readout rarely moves a giant; small biotechs step up for clinical and regulatory events, since a single readout can be the whole story; mid-sized companies are unadjusted. Company size tiers are rough estimates from public knowledge, and borderline calls were re-checked against a market-cap dataset in v3.0.

This is not investment advice. Impact describes how much an event could matter — not which way it will go, and not whether to buy, sell, or hold.

Known blind spots

  • 41.9% of rows (472/1,127) are inferred. ClinicalTrials.gov primary-completion dates do not equal — or guarantee — public topline disclosure.
  • There are zero hard Phase 3 readout dates in this dataset. Hard dates are organizer-confirmed conferences and FDA-grounded dates, including some PDUFAs; clinical readout timing is guidance or inference.
  • No 2027 AdComs are listed because FDA has not posted them yet.
  • H2 2027 PDUFAs remain incomplete until late-2026 FDA acceptances land. The monthly refresh on the 1st of each month is designed to catch them.
  • Every event carries a source link. Official company PR/IR, SEC filings, FDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, and canonical newswires are used wherever they exist. BioSpace, STAT, Endpoints News, similar established biotech outlets, and call transcripts hosted on Quartr are accepted as legitimate sources. Rows that remain on weaker aggregators, wire mirrors, or trade coverage are kept with confidence explicitly flagged in the evidence note; no row is removed for source quality alone.
  • Unguided programs remain on the watchlist rather than receiving invented dates.
